summary: SessionBoard's Call for Papers module runs the full proposal lifecycle: organizers build custom submission forms (multiple field types, required/optional flags, conditional logic that branches by track or session format) with configurable open/close dates, published on a branded public portal. Speakers submit proposals, get automated confirmation emails, and track status. Organizers assign committee reviewers (magic-link invites, caps on reviews per reviewer/submission, field-based filtering); reviewers see an isolated dashboard of only their assigned submissions and score them on customizable scorecards (numeric ratings, text, dropdowns, file uploads) with weighted criteria. Reviews support multiple independent rounds, each with its own scorecard, dates, anonymization (blind review), and reviewer pool. Optional AI Evaluators (configurable reviewer personas with weighted criteria) provide first-pass triage scores with written reasoning; humans can override. Program chairs monitor aggregate scores, reviewer completion rates, and send bulk reminders, then run accept/reject decisions with personalized notification emails. Accepted submissions flow directly into the agenda builder and activate speaker portals with no re-entry. Extras: submission fee collection, COI tracking, full scoring exports, audit trail.
personas: Organizer/Admin (event team building the CFP, managing submissions and decisions)
Program chair (monitors review progress, aggregate scores, makes final decisions)
Speaker/Submitter (submits proposals via public portal, tracks status)

user_journeys.name: Organizer creates and publishes a CFP
steps: Log in to admin, create/open event, go to Call for Papers setup
Build submission form: add fields (text, long text, dropdown, file upload), mark required/optional
Define tracks and session formats; add conditional logic so fields show only for a given track/format
Set submission open and close dates
Publish and copy the public portal link; verify the live form renders
user_journeys.filled_state: Form builder shows ~8-12 fields (title required, abstract, track dropdown with 3 tracks, format dropdown, speaker bio, headshot upload); portal page branded with event name 'DevCon 2026' and a visible deadline

user_journeys.name: Speaker submits a proposal
steps: Fill the form ('Tell us about your session'): title, abstract, track, format, bio
Submit; see confirmation screen and receive confirmation email
Open submitter dashboard, see submission listed with status (e.g. Submitted/Under Review), edit it before the deadline
user_journeys.filled_state: Submitter dashboard lists 1-2 proposals with title, track, and status chips; confirmation banner/email reference visible

user_journeys.name: Reviewer scores assigned submissions
steps: Receive invite (magic link) or sign in as reviewer
Land on review dashboard showing only assigned submissions
Open a submission (anonymized if blind review is on), fill scorecard: numeric ratings per criterion plus comment
Submit review; dashboard shows it as completed and advances to the next assignment
user_journeys.filled_state: Review dashboard shows e.g. '6 assigned, 2 completed'; scorecard has 3 weighted criteria on a 1-5 scale with a comment box; completed items show scores like 4.2/5

user_journeys.name: Chair decides and notifies
steps: Open progress dashboard: submissions count, reviewer completion rates, per-submission aggregate scores
Send bulk reminders to lagging reviewers
Sort by average score; mark top submissions Accepted and others Rejected
Verify accepted submissions became sessions in the agenda/session list and speaker portal invites triggered
user_journeys.filled_state: Submission table with ~10 rows showing avg score column (3.1-4.8), review counts (e.g. 3/3), status column mixing Accepted/Rejected/Under Review; agenda list containing the accepted session titles

features.name: Custom submission form builder
features.description: Organizer builds the CFP form: custom fields of multiple types (text, long text, dropdown, file upload), required/optional flags (title is the only mandatory field), custom question sets per submission type, topic/category configuration.
features.ui_expectations: Admin form-builder screen with add-field controls, field-type picker, required toggle, drag/reorder (inferred), and a live or previewable public form that reflects saved changes.

features.name: Conditional logic and track routing
features.description: Form fields branch on prior answers: track-specific routing, session-format differentiation, different question sets per submission type.
features.ui_expectations: Builder lets a field declare a show-when condition; on the public form, changing the track/format dropdown shows/hides dependent fields without page reload (inferred).

features.name: Public submission portal with open/close dates
features.description: Branded public portal where the CFP is published; organizer configures open and close dates and the portal enforces them (closed state blocks submission).
features.ui_expectations: Public page reachable without admin login, showing event branding, deadline, and the form; after the close date it shows a 'submissions closed' state instead of the form.

features.name: Submitter accounts and dashboard
features.description: Speakers create accounts, submit proposals, and see their own submissions with current status; can edit/withdraw before the deadline (inferred from Sessionize/EasyChair norms).
features.ui_expectations: Sign-up/sign-in on the portal; a 'my submissions' dashboard listing the user's proposals with status labels and an edit action while the CFP is open.

features.name: Automated submission confirmation
features.description: Automated confirmation email sent on submission, plus on-screen confirmation; status update notifications at each process stage.
features.ui_expectations: Confirmation screen/banner after submit; email containing the submission title (verified via inbox or the app's email log if the clone exposes one).

features.name: Reviewer assignment
features.description: Organizer assigns reviewers to submissions with magic-link email invites (no admin accounts needed), configurable max reviews per submission and per reviewer, field-based filtering for targeted assignment, and preview before confirming.
features.ui_expectations: Admin assignment screen mapping reviewers to submissions (manual pick and/or auto-distribute), showing per-reviewer load counts; invited reviewers reach their dashboard via emailed link or login.

features.name: Reviewer dashboard and scorecards
features.description: Reviewers get an isolated dashboard showing only assigned submissions; scorecards support numeric ratings, text responses, dropdowns, and file uploads; submitting a review marks it complete.
features.ui_expectations: Reviewer view lists assigned items with completed/pending state; detail view shows the proposal content plus a scorecard form; no access to unassigned submissions or admin areas.

features.name: Weighted scoring rubrics
features.description: Organizer defines evaluation criteria with relative weights; overall submission score aggregates individual criterion scores per the weights; criteria are customizable per review round.
features.ui_expectations: Rubric config screen listing criteria with weight inputs; submission/aggregate views show per-criterion and overall (weighted) scores consistent with entered ratings.

features.name: Blind (anonymized) review
features.description: Anonymization setting (per round) hides submitter identity from reviewers during evaluation.
features.ui_expectations: Toggle in review-round settings; with it on, reviewer's submission view omits speaker name, email, bio, and photo.

features.name: Multi-round review
features.description: Evaluation plans contain multiple independent rounds (e.g. Initial Review, Final Review, Committee Decision), each with its own scorecard, open/close dates, anonymization setting, and reviewer pool.
features.ui_expectations: Admin can create a second round with a different scorecard and reviewer set; round status (open/closed) shown on a progress dashboard.

features.name: AI Evaluators
features.description: Configurable AI reviewer personas (background, tone, weighted criteria, track focus) give first-pass triage: numeric score plus written reasoning per submission, benchmarked comparisons; human reviewers can override scores.
features.ui_expectations: Persona setup screen (name, expertise, weighted criteria); submissions display an AI score with expandable written rationale alongside human scores, with an override/adjust affordance.

features.name: Progress dashboard and bulk reminders
features.description: Real-time organizer dashboard: submission counts, which rounds are open, reviewer completion rates, bottlenecks; bulk reminder emails to reviewers with outstanding assignments.
features.ui_expectations: Dashboard with counts and per-reviewer completion (e.g. 4/6 done); a 'remind' bulk action; per-submission review-count column.

features.name: Acceptance/rejection workflow
features.description: Committee selection dashboard where chairs view aggregate scores, reviewer comments, and completion rates, then mark submissions Accepted/Rejected/Waitlisted; every stage and decision logged in an audit trail.
features.ui_expectations: Submission table sortable by average score with a status/decision control (per-row and bulk, inferred); status changes reflected in submitter's dashboard.

features.name: Personalized decision notifications
features.description: Personalized acceptance and rejection emails sent from the platform; speaker portal invitations trigger automatically for accepted speakers; email automation at each stage removes manual coordination.
features.ui_expectations: Notification compose/template step with merge fields (inferred), a send action scoped to accepted or rejected sets, and a sent/queued indicator.

features.name: Accepted-to-agenda handoff
features.description: Accepted submissions become sessions in the agenda builder with all metadata intact — no re-entry; speaker portal activation and material collection follow automatically.
features.ui_expectations: After acceptance, the session (same title, speakers, track) appears in the sessions/agenda area ready for scheduling.

features.name: Scoring data export
features.description: Full export of scoring data at every round/stage; shareable reports; natural-language report building (AI reporting).
features.ui_expectations: Export button on review/decision views producing CSV/XLSX containing submissions, per-criterion scores, averages, and statuses.

features.name: Submission fee collection
features.description: Optional payment step inside the form: fee collection via payment gateways, promo codes for invited speakers, VAT config; payment status visible per submission in admin.
features.ui_expectations: Fee amount shown on the form, a payment step at submit, promo-code input, and a paid/unpaid column in the admin submission list.

features.name: Conflict of interest tracking
features.description: COI tracking in committee operations: reviewers declare conflicts and are excluded from scoring those submissions (mechanics inferred from OpenReview/EasyChair norms).
features.ui_expectations: A COI flag/declare action on a reviewer's assigned submission that removes it from their scoring queue and marks it for reassignment.

rubric.criterion: Organizer can build a custom submission form: add fields of at least 3 types (text, dropdown, long text or file upload) and mark fields required/optional; changes appear on the public form
auto_steps: Sign in as organizer/admin
Navigate to CFP/form settings for the event
Add a short-text field 'Key takeaway', a dropdown 'Audience level' with 3 options, mark 'Key takeaway' required; save
Open the public submission form in a fresh context
Confirm both fields render; submit with 'Key takeaway' empty and confirm a required-field validation error
rubric.pass_criteria: All added fields render on the public form with correct types/options; required validation blocks submission when the required field is empty
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of builder with the new fields; screenshot of public form showing them; screenshot of validation error on empty required field

rubric.criterion: Form supports conditional logic: a field configured to show only for a specific track/format appears and disappears based on the submitter's selection
auto_steps: As organizer, add/find a field with a show-when condition tied to one track or session format
Open the public form
Select the triggering track/format and confirm the dependent field appears
Switch to a different track/format and confirm it disappears
rubric.pass_criteria: Dependent field visibility follows the controlling answer in both directions
rubric.evidence: Two screenshots of the public form: one with the condition met (field visible), one without (field hidden)

rubric.criterion: Public portal is reachable without login and enforces configured open/close dates (closed CFP blocks new submissions)
auto_steps: Copy the public portal URL from admin; open it in a logged-out context and confirm the form/event branding loads
As organizer, set the CFP close date to a past datetime; save
Reload the public portal and confirm a closed state (no submittable form)
Restore a future close date and confirm the form is available again
rubric.pass_criteria: Portal loads publicly; past close date yields a closed/blocked state; future date restores submission ability
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of open portal; screenshot of closed-state message after date change

rubric.criterion: A speaker can create a submitter account, complete and submit a proposal, and the submission appears both in their own dashboard and in the organizer's submission list
auto_steps: From the public portal, register a new submitter account (test email)
Fill the form with fixture proposal 'Scaling LLM Inference on a Budget' and submit
Confirm on-screen confirmation
Open the submitter dashboard and confirm the proposal is listed with a status (e.g. Submitted/Under Review)
Sign in as organizer and confirm the same proposal appears in the submissions list with its field values
rubric.pass_criteria: Same submission visible on both sides with matching title and status; data round-trips without loss
rubric.evidence: Screenshots of confirmation screen, submitter dashboard row, and organizer submission detail

rubric.criterion: Submitter can edit an existing submission while the CFP is open, and the change is reflected in the organizer view (norm inferred from Sessionize/EasyChair)
auto_steps: Sign in as the submitter from CFP-04
Open the submitted proposal and edit the abstract text; save
Sign in as organizer and open the submission detail
Confirm the updated abstract text
rubric.pass_criteria: Edited content persists and is what the organizer sees
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of edit form with new text; screenshot of organizer detail showing the same text

rubric.criterion: Submitting a proposal triggers an automated confirmation email to the submitter
rubric.pass_criteria: Human check: submit a proposal using a real/inspectable inbox (or the clone's built-in email log/outbox if present); within a few minutes an email arrives referencing the event and the submitted title. Pass if received with correct submission reference; if the clone exposes an in-app email log, a screenshot of the logged message with correct recipient and title also passes
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of the received email (or in-app email log entry) showing recipient, subject, and submission title

rubric.criterion: Organizer can assign specific submissions to a reviewer, and that reviewer's dashboard shows only assigned submissions (isolation from unassigned ones and admin areas)
auto_steps: As organizer, create/invite a reviewer account and assign it 2 of the 4+ fixture submissions
Sign in as that reviewer (or follow its access link)
Confirm the dashboard lists exactly the 2 assigned submissions
Attempt to reach an unassigned submission (via list or URL manipulation) and confirm it is not accessible
rubric.pass_criteria: Reviewer sees only assigned items; unassigned content and admin functions are inaccessible
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of organizer assignment screen; screenshot of reviewer dashboard showing only the 2 items; screenshot/response of blocked access attempt

rubric.criterion: Reviewer can open an assigned submission and submit a scorecard (at least numeric rating plus text comment); the review is recorded and its completion state updates
auto_steps: As the assigned reviewer, open an assigned submission
Fill the scorecard: numeric ratings per criterion and a comment; submit
Confirm the item now shows as reviewed/completed on the reviewer dashboard
As organizer, open that submission and confirm the score and comment are visible
rubric.pass_criteria: Scores and comment persist, completion state flips, and organizer can see the recorded review
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of filled scorecard; screenshot of completed state; screenshot of organizer view showing score and comment

rubric.criterion: Organizer can define multiple scoring criteria with weights, and the submission's overall score reflects the weighted aggregation of entered ratings
auto_steps: As organizer, configure a rubric with e.g. Relevance 50%, Originality 30%, Speaker experience 20% on a 1-5 scale
As reviewer, score one submission 5/3/1 on those criteria
As organizer, view the submission's overall score
Verify it matches the weighted expectation (5*0.5+3*0.3+1*0.2=3.6) or a documented equivalent aggregation
rubric.pass_criteria: Overall score is a deterministic aggregate consistent with the configured weights (exact weighted mean, or clearly labeled alternative like simple mean only if weights are absent — which fails the weighted requirement)
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of rubric config with weights; screenshot of entered ratings; screenshot of computed overall score

rubric.criterion: Anonymized/blind review setting hides submitter identity (name, email, bio, photo) from the reviewer's view
auto_steps: As organizer, enable anonymization for the review round
As reviewer, open an assigned submission
Inspect the page for the submitter's name/email/bio/photo
Disable anonymization and confirm identity fields reappear
rubric.pass_criteria: With blinding on, no identifying submitter fields render anywhere in the reviewer's submission view; toggling off restores them
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of reviewer view with identity hidden and (after toggle) visible; screenshot of the anonymization setting

rubric.criterion: Review process supports at least two independent rounds with distinct scorecards and/or reviewer pools
auto_steps: As organizer, create Round 2 ('Final Review') with a different scorecard (or different criteria) and a different reviewer set from Round 1
Advance/include at least one submission into Round 2
Sign in as the Round-2 reviewer and confirm the Round-2 scorecard (not Round 1's) is presented
As organizer, confirm both rounds' scores are stored separately
rubric.pass_criteria: Two rounds exist with independent configuration; scores from each round are separately visible
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of round configuration list; screenshot of Round-2 scorecard; screenshot of per-round scores on a submission

rubric.criterion: Organizer dashboard shows review progress: per-reviewer completion (e.g. 2/4 done) and per-submission review counts or aggregate scores
auto_steps: Complete some but not all assigned reviews using the reviewer account
As organizer, open the review progress/monitoring view
Confirm it distinguishes completed vs outstanding reviews per reviewer and shows per-submission review counts or averages
rubric.pass_criteria: Displayed completion numbers match the actual reviews performed in earlier steps
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of progress dashboard with counts matching the known review state

rubric.criterion: Organizer can set accept/reject decisions on submissions; status updates in the admin list and in the submitter's own dashboard
auto_steps: As organizer, mark one fixture submission Accepted and another Rejected (per-row control or bulk action)
Confirm the admin list shows the new statuses
Sign in as each affected submitter and confirm their dashboard reflects Accepted/Rejected respectively
rubric.pass_criteria: Both decisions persist and propagate to the correct submitter accounts
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of admin list with mixed statuses; screenshots of each submitter dashboard showing the correct status

rubric.criterion: Platform sends (or queues) personalized acceptance and rejection notification emails to decided submitters
auto_steps: As organizer, after CFP-13, invoke the notify/send-decisions action (choosing or confirming accept and reject templates if prompted)
Confirm the UI reports the messages as sent/queued (e.g. sent count, per-submission notified indicator, or email log entries)
rubric.pass_criteria: UI confirms decision notifications were dispatched to the right recipient sets; NOT auto-verified: actual email delivery and personalization of body content — a human should check a real inbox for one acceptance and one rejection message naming the submission
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of the send/notify flow and the sent/queued confirmation; (manual supplement) screenshot of received accept and reject emails

rubric.criterion: Accepting a submission makes it available as a session in the agenda/session management area with its metadata (title, speaker, track) intact, without re-entry
auto_steps: Accept a submission (from CFP-13) and follow any 'convert to session'/'move to agenda' affordance if presented
Navigate to the sessions/agenda area of the event
Confirm a session exists with the same title, speaker, and track as the accepted submission
rubric.pass_criteria: Accepted submission's data appears as a session record without manual re-typing of its fields
rubric.evidence: Screenshot of accepted submission detail; screenshot of the matching session in the agenda/session list

rubric.criterion: Organizer can export scoring/submission data (CSV/XLSX) containing submissions, scores, and statuses
rubric.pass_criteria: Human check: click the export action on the submissions/review view, open the downloaded file, and verify it contains one row per submission with title, per-criterion or average scores, and decision status matching the on-screen data. Pass if the file opens and the known fixture rows/values are present and correct
rubric.evidence: The downloaded file plus a screenshot of the on-screen table it should match

sample_data: Event: "DevCon 2026" (CFP open now, closes 2026-10-01). Tracks: "AI & ML", "Web Platform", "Engineering Leadership". Session formats: Talk (30 min), Workshop (90 min), Panel (45 min). Form fields: Session title* (text), Abstract* (long text ~150 words), Track* (dropdown), Format* (dropdown), Key takeaway (text, required — added in CFP-01), Audience level (dropdown: Beginner/Intermediate/Advanced), Speaker bio (long text), Headshot (file), conditional field "Workshop prerequisites" shown only when Format=Workshop. Rubric: Relevance 50%, Originality 30%, Speaker experience 20%, scale 1-5. Fixture submissions (6): "Scaling LLM Inference on a Budget" (AI & ML, Talk), "Postgres as Your Message Queue" (Web Platform, Talk), "Hands-on WebGPU" (Web Platform, Workshop), "From IC to Manager and Back" (Engineering Leadership, Talk), "Evals That Actually Catch Regressions" (AI & ML, Workshop), "Panel: The Future of Frontend" (Web Platform, Panel). Accounts: organizer admin@devcon.test; submitters alice@example.test (2 proposals), bob@example.test, carol@example.test; reviewers rev1@devcon.test, rev2@devcon.test, rev3@devcon.test. Decisions for testing: accept "Scaling LLM Inference...", reject "Postgres as Your Message Queue".
gaps: Marketing pages do not specify: submitter draft-saving and post-submission edit rules (inferred from Sessionize/EasyChair norms — CFP-05 marked as inferred norm); co-speaker/co-author invitation flow mechanics; notification template editor details and merge fields (inferred); bulk decision actions (inferred); waitlist status existence; exact reviewer auth model for the CFP product (magic-link detail comes from the abstract-management page and may differ); COI declaration mechanics (only named on a compare page, mechanics inferred from OpenReview norms — excluded from rubric as too speculative); AI Evaluator configuration UI specifics (feature documented but left out of the rubric since clones may legitimately stub AI). No actual product screenshots were inspectable as images — UI expectations derive from captions/alt-text and category norms. Pricing/tier gating of features unknown.
